picks.file: View of Algiers and its Bay in the XVI century.jpg
picks.what: Bird’s-eye view, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 2
picks.why: clean hand-colored copy; walled city with the mole and the island fort; legend box cut; record’s 1540 is Braun’s birth year

picks.file: Gezicht op Algiers met De Ruyters schip 'De Liefde', 1662, SK-A-1396.jpg
picks.what: View from the sea with De Ruyter’s ship De Liefde, painting (Rijksmuseum)
picks.why: color view of the white walled town climbing its hill above the harbor

picks.file: Gezicht op Algiers De Stad Algiers (titel op object), RP-P-1909-1656.jpg
picks.why: panorama of the town and the coast with ships; trimmed toward the town, title and legend cut

picks.file: View of Algiers from the Sea LCCN2006683443.tif
picks.what: View from the sea, aquatint (Library of Congress)
picks.why: the classic white triangle of the town, mole and lighthouse; 56 years after the 1762 view; title and margins cut

picks.what: The harbor and the waterfront from the Admiralty, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: harbor with the arcaded boulevard and the white city rising up the hill behind
whole city from above with the Casbah’s dense triangle and the harbor

picks.what: View over the Casbah to the bay, photograph
picks.why: sharp color view across the old town roofs to the harbor

notes: #17 is the weaker of the two P3 views (small town in a wide panorama); drop it if only strong views should double up. Skipped Humbert de Molard’s paper negatives (#19, #20): damaged, dated only 1845–53, and the place is hard to confirm. Other P4 options: #23 (bay from Notre-Dame d’Afrique) and #21/#24 (from Mustapha), both general views where the old town is less visible. #37 is Algiers, Louisiana.
